clue.text: Old rulers establish spies in Spain

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for the country sits inside the word for secret agents

blocks.note: to plant something is to set it up firmly
spies are secret agents
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A dynasty of old kings sets up a spy network in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the international vehicle code for Spain, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the royal house that held the English throne from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Bird has drink trouble

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of beer, a drink
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A bird gets into difficulty over drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintado is a name for the guineafowl and also the Cape petrel, both birds.

clue.text: Other transport used in Spain after rail disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters of the track word are thrown about
after sends the phrase meaning located in Spain to follow the wrecked track word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: After a train crash in Spain, travellers switch to another way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used in Spain' reads as part of the story, but 'in' is literal and Spain is the vehicle code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company offering travel by plane, a form of transport other than the railway.

clue.text: Tory paper offered one for nothing to circulate in Ireland

definitions.note: the answer is a place in Ireland; the definition names only its location

indicators.note: offering one thing for another means swapping it in, here a numeral one in place of a zero-shaped letter
circulating sends the letters moving round into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Conservative newspaper is handed out free to readers across Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the O of TORY PAPER for I, then rearrange to get TIPPERARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a county and town in the Irish province of Munster, famous from the wartime song.

clue.text: Boy given to exuberance

blocks.note: Gus is a boy's name, short for Angus or Augustus
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad prone to high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and zest, close in meaning to lively exuberance.

clue.text: Scot turns up with tailless bird in Africa

definitions.note: the answer is a city in Africa; the definition names only its location

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the Scottish name from bottom to top
without a tail the bird loses its final letter

blocks.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scottish name
the robin is a common garden bird

explanation.surface: A Scotsman arrives in Africa carrying a bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN read upwards is NAI, and ROBIN without its last letter is ROBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya in East Africa.

clue.text: Plug First Telecom's  current charge

indicators.note: First asks for only the opening letter of the company name

blocks.note: the opening letter of the company name
an amp is the unit of electric current
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A phone company's electricity tariff, as in a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends 'current charge' is the price on a bill; current and charge are separate electrical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tampion is a wooden stopper put in the muzzle of a gun, so it is a kind of plug.

clue.text: Male gender reconstructed in colour - of 3?

definitions.note: 3 is TIPPERARY, in Ireland, the Emerald Isle, whose colour this is

indicators.note: the word splits as re plus constructed, and something constructed is assembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first two letters of the word that carries the rearranging instruction

explanation.surface: A sex change pictured in vivid colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram needs RE as well as MALE GENDER, and it comes from the word 'reconstructed' itself: RE plus 'constructed'. Ireland is called the Emerald Isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald green is the bright green shade associated with Ireland, home of the cross-referenced county.

clue.text: Incantation against poacher's first peril

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the trespassing hunter's title

blocks.note: a mantra is a chanted word or phrase
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A magic spell chanted to ward off a poacher is the first danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' means next to, placing the letter beside the chant; a mantrap is just what landowners once set against poachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a hidden snare to catch trespassers, a hazard or danger to anyone who stumbles on it.

clue.text: "Like it could bring the house down", audibly breathes the Irishman with regret

definitions.text: Like it could bring the house down

indicators.note: audibly says the following words are to be heard, not read

blocks.note: one sighs by breathing out heavily, especially with regret
Mick is a stock Irish name

explanation.surface: An Irishman sighs ruefully over a performance that brought the house down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With regret' explains the kind of breathing meant: sighs. Said together, sighs and Mick sound like SEISMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic describes earthquakes, which literally can bring a house down, and figuratively anything huge.

clue.text: Religious establishment on island left according to custom

blocks.note: a convent is a community of nuns
Iona is a small Scottish island, an early Christian centre
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A nunnery on a remote island follows its traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is not I but IONA, fitting the religious surface: St Columba founded a monastery there.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional means following accepted custom or usual practice.

clue.text: Twig for cash

definitions.note: the definition is a fragment of the phrase 'realise for cash', fair because that phrase is the standard idiom for selling assets

blocks.note: first meaning: to grasp or understand, informally
second meaning: to convert assets into money

explanation.walkthrough: Twig looks like a small branch but is the slang verb for catching on.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to become aware of something and to sell property or assets to obtain money.

clue.text: Cubist varsity type?

blocks.note: surface reading: an artist of the Picasso and Braque school
setter's reading: a university member from a city named after young cattle crossing a ford, cubs of the ox

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags whimsy: 'Cubist' is stretched to mean a young-ox person, and the varsity is the one in the city named for oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a member or graduate of Oxford University, the city's name coming from a river crossing for cattle.

clue.text: Licentious spectacles in college

indicators.note: in puts the eyewear letters inside the abbreviation for the college

blocks.note: the London School of Economics, a college of London University
two round lenses look like a pair of Os

explanation.surface: Racy behaviour by bespectacled students at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles as OO is a crossword convention: the two lenses look like two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose person in the old moral sense is promiscuous or dissolute, which is what licentious means.

clue.text: One can work in computer apparatus

indicators.note: work as a verb means the letters are worked over into a new shape
in places the reworked letters inside the brand of computer

blocks.note: Apple is a well-known computer maker
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can operate a computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One can work' reads like a claim of competence, but 'work' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or piece of equipment for a particular task, much as apparatus is.

clue.text: Average sum - there's nothing better

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the adjective supreme

blocks.note: par is the normal or average level
an amount is a total or sum

explanation.surface: A middling total, and yet it is boasted as unbeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of the highest importance, so nothing ranks above it.

clue.text: Opponent wins over philosopher

blocks.note: to gain someone is to win them over
A. J. Ayer was a twentieth-century British philosopher

explanation.surface: A rival debater persuades a philosopher to change sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A gainsayer is one who contradicts or denies, someone who argues against you.

clue.text: Setter is out of date - you can't escape that

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself says I'm
passé means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: The compiler ruefully admits being behind the times, and there's no way round it.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' often means I or ME, the compiler himself; 'setter is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or dead end, a situation offering no way out or progress.

clue.text: One could be converted to saint - eg Pancras?

definitions.note: St Pancras is a major London railway terminus

indicators.note: converted plays on religious conversion while meaning the letters are changed into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sinner might be converted into a saint, as Pancras was.
explanation.walkthrough: Pancras looks like the saint himself, but the definition is the London station St Pancras.
explanation.definitionFit: St Pancras is a famous London railway terminus, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: Close to being the opposite of 13

blocks.note: first meaning: near, snug, closely fitting
second meaning: the antonym of the answer at 13 across

explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is LOOSE, and the word for its opposite also means close, as in a close or tight finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight describes something firmly fixed or close-fitting, the reverse of slack or loose.

clue.text: A casual worker with time to paint

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A temporary hand is given some time to do the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by mixing pigment with egg yolk, used by early Renaissance artists.

clue.text: Range from cosy turning to torrid

indicators.note: turning means the word for cosy is turned round and read backwards

blocks.note: snug means warm and cosy
torrid means very hot

explanation.surface: The temperature scale runs from comfortably warm to scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: Range looks like a span of temperatures, but it is the distance a gun can fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunshot can mean the distance reached by a fired bullet, as in 'within gunshot', i.e. range.

clue.text: Account for one's involvement in abandoned scheme

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it, so the numeral goes within the scheme words

blocks.note: ex means former, given up
a scheme is a plan
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone must justify their part in a scheme that was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, meaning former, is a common crossword piece for abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to explain an event is to give reasons or a justification for why it happened.

clue.text: River explored by retired major general

indicators.note: something explored by the officer lies within his words, waiting to be found
retired means withdrawn, so the run of letters is read going backwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A river charted by a senior officer now in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Victorian explorer; the river name hides backwards across majOR GENeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negro is a major South American river, a large tributary of the Amazon.

clue.text: It's the same in France - not unusual for a souvenir

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the negative word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: même is French for same
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French tourist shrugs that a souvenir is the same everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event, a keepsake.

clue.text: Settling in gent's outfit

indicators.note: outfit as a verb means to fit out afresh, so the letters are refitted in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting comfortable in a man's suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Outfit looks like a noun, clothes, but works as the rearranging verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting is what birds do when building a home and making themselves at home, i.e. settling down.

clue.text: Arthur English somehow used to pass water

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: the duct used for this

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An Englishman called Arthur once relieved himself somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur English was a British comedian, which makes the surface read as a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the duct through which urine leaves the body.

clue.text: Cooking of Anne's to brag about?

definitions.text: Cooking of Anne's to brag about?

indicators.note: cooking means mixing things up, so the following letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to brag about something is to boast of it

explanation.surface: Is Anne's cooking really anything to show off about?
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is ironic: the question mark doubts that this humble dish is anything to brag about.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans on toast is a basic British snack of baked beans heaped on toasted bread, typical humble home cooking.
